aAbout: Sentinel Hub is a cloud-based service, run by Sinergise Solutions — a Planet Labs company — that makes satellite data from the Sentinels, Landsat and other providers easy to browse or analyse, in its cloud GIS or in your own environment. Its documentation describes 7 APIs for searching, processing, analysing, visualising and downloading satellite data and integrating it into your own application, metered in processing units (PU). Its data spans Sentinel-1, 2, 3 and 5P, the Landsat archive, commercial Planet and Maxar collections, elevation models and bring-your-own-data collections. Its free showcase app is EO Browser; the platform itself is a paid subscription product with a 30-day free trial, and an account is required for API use.
aStrengths: Sentinel Hub is the buildable platform: 7 APIs — Processing, Batch Processing, Catalog (STAC-based), Statistical, OGC and more — plus a Python package, QGIS and ArcGIS integration via OGC services, custom evalscripts, multi-temporal processing and bring-your-own-data collections, across Sentinel, Landsat and commercial Planet and Maxar data. If satellite imagery needs to end up inside your own application, pipeline or product, Copernicus Browser cannot do that job and Sentinel Hub was built for exactly it.
bAbout: Copernicus Browser is the free visual front end of the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, the European programme's open ecosystem for Earth-observation data. Official documentation describes it as a central hub for accessing, exploring and using data from the Copernicus Sentinel constellations and more — and states plainly that it is based on Sentinel Hub's EO Browser technology. It visualises Sentinel-1, 2, 3 and 5P data and two digital elevation models, with ready-made and custom visualisations, spectral indices such as NDVI, a compare tool, pins, 3D visualisation, statistical tools and timelapse export as GIF or MPEG4. It is completely free; a free account is currently required to use it, and it is web only.
bStrengths: Copernicus Browser is the same viewing technology with the price and the sales process removed: completely free, with no paid plans at all, covering Sentinel-1, 2, 3 and 5P plus elevation models, with true- and false-colour rendering, NDVI and custom indices, compare mode, pins, 3D views, statistics and timelapse export built in. For anyone who wants to look at, compare, analyse in the browser and download Sentinel imagery — students, journalists, researchers, the curious — it does the viewing job in full, for €0.
betterAnswer: It depends on whether imagery is something you look at or something you build with. Copernicus Browser is better for looking: the free official viewer, built on Sentinel Hub's own EO Browser technology, with Sentinel data, indices, compare mode and timelapses for €0. Sentinel Hub is better for building: the paid developer platform whose 7 APIs, processing-unit subscriptions and commercial data collections feed your own applications. Viewers should start — and may never need to leave — Copernicus Browser; developers who outgrow a viewer graduate to Sentinel Hub.

faqs.a: In effect, yes for viewing: the official Copernicus Data Space documentation states that Copernicus Browser is based on Sentinel Hub's EO Browser, which Sentinel Hub itself describes as its free web application showcasing its functionality. Copernicus Browser is the European ecosystem's official, completely free version of that viewing experience.
faqs.q: Is Copernicus Browser built on Sentinel Hub technology?

faqs.a: Not as a platform. Sentinel Hub offers a 30-day free trial that includes API-level access, and its EO Browser showcase app is free to use — but ongoing API use sits behind paid subscriptions metered in processing units. Copernicus Browser, by contrast, is completely free with no paid plans.

No public price can be stated: on 2026-10-29 Sentinel Hub's pricing page redirected to Planet's pricing page, which lists no Sentinel Hub plan prices and routes buyers to contact sales. What is public is the structure — subscriptions metered in processing units, with published allowances such as Exploration at 30,000 PU per month (non-commercial), Basic up to 70,000 PU per month and Enterprise S at 400,000 PU per month.
faqs.q: How much does Sentinel Hub cost?

faqs.a: Yes. ESA's guide calls it a free and easy tool, the Data Space describes free instant access under Copernicus's free and open data policy, and there are no paid plans, subscriptions or pricing pages for the Browser. The only requirement is a free account, which is currently needed to use it.
faqs.q: Is Copernicus Browser really completely free?

faqs.a: For Sentinel Hub, yes — its documentation states you need a Sentinel Hub account to work with its APIs, and the 30-day trial also requires sign-up. For Copernicus Browser, the official documentation states that you currently need a free account to use the Browser. Neither account costs money to create.
faqs.q: Do I need an account for either tool?

faqs.a: Sentinel Hub. It is the developer platform — 7 APIs including Processing, Batch, Catalog (STAC-based), Statistical and OGC, a Python package and GIS integrations — metered in processing units on paid subscriptions. Copernicus Browser is a viewer for people, not a platform for code, although the wider Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem documents APIs of its own.
faqs.q: Which should a developer choose, Sentinel Hub or Copernicus Browser?

intro: Sentinel Hub and Copernicus Browser share DNA — literally. Copernicus Browser, the completely free official viewer of the Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem, is built on Sentinel Hub's EO Browser technology. What separates them is what surrounds the viewer. Sentinel Hub, run by Sinergise, a Planet Labs company, is the paid developer platform: 7 APIs, subscriptions metered in processing units, Landsat and commercial Planet and Maxar data on top of the Sentinels. Copernicus Browser is the viewer set free: Sentinel-1, 2, 3 and 5P visualisations, indices, compare mode and timelapses for €0, with only a free account asked. It is the classic split — the API, or the free viewer built on the same tech.
pricingA: Paid subscriptions metered in processing units — but no public prices exist: on 2026-10-29 Sentinel Hub's pricing page redirected to Planet's pricing page, which lists no Sentinel Hub plan prices and routes buyers to contact sales, so no euro or dollar price is stated here. The published structure is processing-unit allowances — Exploration 30,000 PU per month (which does not support commercial use), Basic up to 70,000 PU per month, and Enterprise S 400,000 PU per month — with monthly and annual packages described in its FAQ. A 30-day free trial includes API-level access, and its EO Browser showcase app is free to use.
pricingB: Completely free — €0, with no paid plans, subscriptions or pricing pages. The Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem describes free instant access under Copernicus's free and open data policy. The only requirement is a free account, which the official documentation states is currently needed to use the Browser.

verdictA: Choose Sentinel Hub if you build with satellite data — feeding imagery into your own application, pipeline or product through its APIs, running custom processing at scale, or adding Landsat and commercial Planet and Maxar collections beyond the Sentinels.
verdictB: Choose Copernicus Browser if you look at satellite data — studying vegetation with NDVI, comparing a place across dates, making timelapses, or downloading Sentinel imagery for a report or classroom, without paying anything or talking to a sales team.
verdictLine: Sentinel Hub is the platform you build on; Copernicus Browser is the viewer you open. Same EO Browser roots — one is metered by processing units behind a contact-sales wall, the other is the European programme's gift: the viewing job done in full, for free.
worldEye: Both tools show the Earth from orbit, as data. WorldEye shows it from the ground, live: a free 3D globe that opens in any browser with no signup — 74,229 public cameras across 105 countries, alongside live flights, ships, satellites, weather, earthquakes and wildfires in the same view. It offers neither Sentinel Hub's APIs nor Copernicus Browser's Sentinel analysis, and it does not claim to; it is the live-planet view. Its optional Pro tier is $7.99/week, $13.99/month or $74.99/year.
